title: A line that moves
bodyMd:
A river authority's flood map places properties into risk bands based on estimated water levels and the height of the surrounding land. When a new elevation survey became available, several properties moved into a higher band even though no new building had occurred and the river's channel had not changed. Some owners interpreted the revised map as evidence that the river itself had suddenly become more dangerous.

The authority explained that the earlier survey had rounded ground heights too coarsely in a low-lying neighbourhood. More precise measurements changed the estimate of exposure. The revised classification could affect planning decisions, but the date of a revised estimate was not necessarily the date of a physical change. Better knowledge of a longstanding condition can alter an official category without creating the condition.
